body: Tag edits from the Properties window (the TagWriter contract) and per-directory view-preference writes (persist_view_preferences, navigate_with_column_parent) still lock and rewrite the catalog file on the UI thread when the user edits them. Escalation 54ca2f0b answered that this commitment leaves them; move them to background tasks and give the Properties window an asynchronous writer.
title: Promote catalog-writes-off-ui-thread

subject: UXF-023 is implemented and checked for every path the roadmap names: navigation, view preferences, Properties tag edits, sidebar tag rename and delete, pin checks, Home orphan cleanup and move completion leave the UI thread, and every catalog write runs in the one write queue

body: The menu composition state lives in five interior-mutability fields (composing_menu, pending_store_probes, pending_menu_recompose, render_probes, probes_in_flight) with three take or move paths (take_pending_menu_probe, move_menu_probes_to_render, flush_render_probes). A composition that forgets take_pending_menu_probe leaves its probes and recompose for the next menu. Fold them into one composition record that a menu opens and closes, so a forgotten take cannot happen (adversary report 9fa1a7b3, finding 12).
title: Promote menu-composition-state
wrong_if: the item is not covered by the Agreed requirements its roadmap section names

subject: the menu composition state is one StoreProbeQueue with a private MenuComposition record that each composition opens and closes; a menu composed without a popup hands its probes to the next frame and leaves nothing for the next menu; UXF-023 passes

body: When the native-theme bridge cannot read the system theme, install_native_theme installs the fallback preset for the window appearance at install time only; a later switch between dark and light keeps the old variant until the next start. Observe the window appearance (Window::observe_window_appearance) and install the fallback again on a change (adversary report 9fa1a7b3, finding 11).
title: Promote fallback-theme-follows-appearance-changes
wrong_if: the item is not covered by the Agreed requirements its roadmap section names

subject: UIV-014: while the Adwaita fallback is in use, every browser window installs the variant of the appearance it opens with and follows each later switch between dark and light; a system theme installed later ends the fallback

body: A tag write's extended-attribute I/O (apply_tag_delta, tags_for's import, reconcile_pending_xattrs) runs inside the catalog write queue job, so a tagged file on a hung mount holds every later catalog write, from every window, until the mount answers. The UI thread and the directory models keep working; catalog writes wait. Split the intent protocol into steps: stage the desired tags in a queued job, write the attribute in its own background task, then finish or restage the record in another queued job, keeping the order against other tag writes. Review 54e960e8 finding 4 on catalog-writes-off-ui-thread.
title: Promote xattr-io-outside-catalog-queue
wrong_if: the item is not covered by the Agreed requirements its roadmap section names

subject: UXF-024: extended-attribute reads and writes run on per-mount attribute lanes, never in the catalog write queue or on its thread pool; the catalog records a tag change before its attribute write, and a mount whose store blocks holds only its own lane

title: RSA keys only through the SSH agent
wrong_if: a user's only SFTP key is an RSA key file they cannot load into an agent, or the rsa crate's advisory RUSTSEC-2023-0071 is fixed and RSA key files become safe to sign with

title: Supersede remote-usable with remote-usable-extract
wrong_if: the developer did not choose this successor

subject: SFTP signs with RSA keys only through the SSH agent, asking for SHA-512 or SHA-256; RSA key files and stored RSA keys are refused with KeyNeedsAgent (sftp.rs decode_login_key, login_with_agent; SYS-032 receipt c59d9893)

body: Read it as SSH agent login Instead: Read the missing field as password login and show the connection as needing a login method.
rests_on: Before this commitment such a profile opened through OpenDAL's system-ssh service, which logged in with the user's agent, default keys and ~/.ssh/config (0c979d6 crates/musheen-desktop/src/remote/sftp.rs:67-84). The new wire format reads a missing login field as SshLogin::Password, and a password login with no stored password sends only the none method, so each such connection that browsed before now fails (adversary report 4c4ba543 finding 8). Agent login keeps the agent part of the old behavior; SYS-032 names agent login as one of the four methods.
title: How should an SFTP connection saved by an older build, with no login method and no stored password, log in now?
wrong_if: A connection whose server wanted a default key file outside the agent still fails, as it does today, and the user picks Private key file in the editor.

subject: An SFTP profile saved with no login field and no stored password reads as agent login; SFTP profiles always write their login (connection.rs legacy_login; dd78c72, 9e58451; SYS-032 receipt 3461ef24)

remote-usable-extract carries remote-usable's work and builds the revised OPS-033: Extract… and Extract Here extract into a folder named after the archive and ask Replace, Replace All, Skip or Skip All for each collision (c91776f, eca7016; OPS-033 receipt eb21cc6b)

body: The global remote.credential setting is still in the settings schema and shown on the Integrations page, but since remote-usable-extract nothing reads it: each connection stores its own password under its ID. Profiles an older build saved may still reference that global secret, and the editor now keeps such a reference. Retire the setting with a settings migration that leaves those references working, and drop its read-only row (adversary report 4c4ba543 finding 18).
title: Promote retire-global-remote-credential
wrong_if: the item is not covered by the Agreed requirements its roadmap section names

subject: The global remote.credential setting and its read-only row are gone from the schema, the Integrations page, settings search and the three locales (75b443d). No migration was written: as SYS-033 says, an older file keeps the value as an unknown key, unread, and a connection that refers to that secret keeps its reference and logs in with it (5833923; SYS-033 receipt 7b2e6d1a)

body: Encode broker listings compactly (names as base64 or length-prefixed bytes instead of JSON arrays of numbers) and stop reading a folder once its listing passes the 64 MiB bound, with an error that names the size limit. Today names cost about four bytes per byte, so a folder whose names total about 16 MiB is refused, and the root broker builds the whole listing before it checks the size (elevated-session report finding 5).
title: Promote compact-broker-listings
wrong_if: the item is not covered by the Agreed requirements its roadmap section names

subject: Broker listings send each entry as a JSON array with its name and identity in base64 and no key names; the broker counts each entry's encoded bytes as it reads a folder and stops past 64 MiB with listing-too-large, which the elevated window shows in the user's language, naming the limit (7401107, dbef7a3; SYS-034 receipt c72beecb)

body: Broker listings changed their wire format in compact-broker-listings with no protocol version. A Musheen still running after a package upgrade starts the new broker for its next Open as Administrator: the window opens, then every listing fails with the general error, and the session and its root broker stay up until the window closes, Musheen exits, or 15 minutes pass without a request. Put a protocol version in the broker's first answer, refuse a mismatch with a message that tells the user to restart Musheen, and end the session when a response cannot be decoded (adversary report 78c7cc31 finding 4).
title: Promote broker-protocol-version
wrong_if: the item is not covered by the Agreed requirements its roadmap section names

subject: Musheen and its broker share protocol version 1: Musheen reads the installed broker's version before any authorization is asked for, the broker names it before it reads its request, a mismatch says to restart Musheen and leaves no broker running, and an answer Musheen cannot read ends the session

body: crates/musheen-ui/tests/elevated_browser.rs elevated_session_lists_to_the_limit_and_names_it_beyond lists 170,000 names (about 65 MB) through the fake broker with a 10 s backend timeout and asserts it finishes within 10 s. On 2026-09-28 it failed once in the workspace run (Polkit: 'the elevated broker could not read this location', the ExecutionTimedOut fallback) while another project built with 12 jobs (load average about 8); it passed 3 of 3 reruns of the same binary at load about 5 (19 s per run of the four listing tests). Make the test independent of machine load (a longer test-only timeout, or measure the broker's own time), or give the fallback message the timeout's cause.
